subject: Sandbox rev-share pilot: Observify + Redwood integration
messages:

Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood + Observify sandbox pilot interest

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the quick intro call yesterday. Observify is excited to explore a co-sell sandbox and a short rev-share pilot that demonstrates end-to-end telemetry + LLM inference value for our joint customers. High-level ask from our side:

- A 6-8 week sandbox where we can route OTLP metrics/traces through Observify into Redwood’s inference pipeline for a small sample of customers (synthetic traffic OK).
- Joint demo + one case study if metrics and latency targets are achieved.
- Simple rev-share for any conversion from the sandbox to paid Redwood Dedicated seats.

I attached a short one-pager that covers our go-to-market model and some customer logos (observify-onepager.pdf).

Can you loop in the right Redwood folks for technical fit and commercial terms? We’re targeting a mid-Apr kickoff window.

Best,
Samira Patel

Thanks Samira — looping in Ben, Laura, and Neha to scope the sandbox and commercial approach. Quick summary of what I heard and asks for the internal team below.

Summary of Observify ask:
1) 6-week sandbox to validate telemetry ingestion + end-to-end demo.
2) Joint case study if we hit latency & quality thresholds.
3) A simple rev-share model for leads that convert to Dedicated seats.

Internal asks / initial questions:
- Ben: feasibility for an OTLP relay -> Redwood hosted test environment (throughput target ~ 2000 req/min, sample retention 1 day).
- Neha: security/compliance gating — Observify will likely ask for SOC2 questionnaire + ephemeral data retention.
- Laura: commercial construct — what rev-share bands make sense for a pilot? (we can propose simple 20/80 referral splits for closed deals under $50k ARR, subject to legal)

Samira — can you confirm your preferred trial region (US or EU) and whether you need a sandbox Datadog org created, or you’ll bring your own? Also copying potential vendor contacts at Datadog and Grafana if we need platform-level coordination.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical kickoff this week to lock scope.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
tessa@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@observify.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood + Observify sandbox pilot interest

Tessa / team — quick technical read: this is feasible but we should scope tight to keep infra cost low. Notes: 

- Ingestion path: Observify can push OTLP to a lightweight relay we host in the sandbox VPC. We can run an OTLP adapter that forwards sampled spans/metrics into a test inference route.
- Keys/credentials: prefer short-lived tokens (we can mint via console).
- Throughput: 2k req/min is fine for the initial two-week ramp; suggest we cap at 5k to protect shared infra.
- Metrics to validate: request latency p50/p95 to backend inference, token cost per request, and end-to-end error rate.

Attached is a starter ops checklist for the sandbox: sandbox-ops-checklist.xlsx. I also sketched a minimal mutual action plan below: 

Mutual Action Plan (MVP):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + security intake (Observify provides SOC2, AEs sign NDA if needed).
2) Week 1–2: Provision sandbox, create test Datadog org (if needed), deploy OTLP relay.
3) Week 3–5: Run POC traffic, collect metrics, iterate on batching/kv-caching to hit cost targets.
4) Week 6: Demo + metrics review + decision (expand or close).

Commercial note: pilot rev-share proposal is fine as a starting point but legal needs to draft a short MoA (memorandum of agreement). I’ll drop the ops-owner for rollout once we commit.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Hi Tessa / Samira —

Datadog can stand up a trial org for Observify to ingest telemetry; a couple of quick items to note:

- Region: US (us3) is recommended for low latency to Redwood’s west coast test infra.
- API/ingest keys: we’ll create short-lived ingest keys scoped to the trial org.
- Agent/plugin: if you plan to forward OTLP directly, we suggest using the OTLP exporter to avoid double-processing.

I attached a short playbook describing ingestion best practices and cost controls (datadog-playbook.md). If you want, I can provision the trial org today — please confirm which email to use for admin and whether Observify will populate synthetic traffic or we should provide a load script.

On cost controls: please enable metric rollups at 1m and use sampling for traces to reduce billable volume during the pilot.

-Joe
